title: Guards, and the first case that matches

blocks.text: A guard narrows a type pattern: `case Integer i when i < 0 ->`. The cases are tried from the top, and the first one that matches wins, so when two guarded cases overlap, the narrower one comes first. An unguarded `case Integer i` then catches every remaining `Integer`.
Write `classify(Object obj)` in `Classifier` as one switch expression, after the page's own example:

cases.says: 0 is "Zero": its case comes before the wider small-positive guard.
NaN is "Not a number" and the infinities are "Infinite".

concepts: Overlapping cases are tried in order and the first that matches wins, so narrower guards come first.
A when guard narrows a type pattern with a condition on the pattern variable.
